action_items.item: Switch flags such as monthly-spend-feature on for a small share of traffic first, and widen it in steps rather than for all traffic at once.
Hold or reverse a flag rollout automatically when the service's error rate rises after the flag changes.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix proposed in PR #363 is in production.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is told when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests that failed rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average, with a worst of {errors_at_worst}, and the service's own warnings showed the account page error rate at its highest at {Gbac1.7}.

Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appeared at the onset and was logged {G5309.1} times during {G5309.3}. Before the onset, the only account page error logged was a shopper closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: no deploys came back for the day before the onset, and the flag toggle was the only production change read.
Any other flag change: the flag provider's history showed only the one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read.
A rollout still in progress: as of {T10.1}, all replicas were running one revision.

causal_chain.step: At {P1.1}, admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature. Before that, every evaluation came back off and account pages rendered normally. In the minute {G971b.6}, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and every evaluation after that came back on. Switching the flag back off brought the service back from the incident's level, and that action was judged confirmed.

Code-Fix read that, with the flag on, the account page's spend summary divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of items bought this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division fails at line {F1.1}, the line the logged error points to.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending summary on account pages, and it likely tried to divide by the number of items the shopper had bought this month, which cannot work for shoppers who have bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag reached almost all account page traffic at once. In the first minute, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and after that every evaluation came back on. No staged rollout, and no automatic hold on a rise in errors, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Turning the flag on for a small share of traffic first would have limited the failures to that share, and the rise in errors could have been caught before it reached most shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the monthly spend summary for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix had to write new cases to cover it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have failed on the division before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: Argus traced the failures to the flag change and switched monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed, {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened a draft fix, PR #363, {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so no person was told while the incident ran.

input.root_cause: The account page's monthly spend summary, which runs only when monthly-spend-feature is on, divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of items bought this month (line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py). For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list of items is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The failing code path was left unchanged when the flag was switched off, so turning monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
